title: Errors of up to 11.50 km at three depth labels can remove the ComCat median depth decrease in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested the error limit needed to remove a reported median depth decrease in 12,848 global ComCat earthquakes with preferred M >= 5.5. The median fell from 28.40 km in 2000-2012 to 15.91 km in 2013-2025. We allowed errors only at exact 10, 33 and 35 km labels and held all other depths fixed. Sharp interval bounds first permit zero median change at a common error limit of 11.50 km. An endpoint assignment gives a median of 21.50 km in both periods. With a 10 km error limit, all assignments still give at least a 3.00 km decrease. With a 15 km limit, either sign is possible. If errors are allowed at all depths, the critical limit falls to 6.245 km. These are finite-sample sensitivity bounds, not measured errors or a physical depth trend. Unchecked errors outside the labels, mixed sources, selected periods and catalog revisions limit inference. The bundle gives original code, aggregate bounds, source hashes, an independent count audit, a figure and reproduction instructions. External event records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Sharp median change bounds for stated error limits. Other depths are held fixed in each selected-record model. These are permitted ranges, not confidence intervals.
